name: Mustardseed
description: The most majestic and sophisticated city in Tanares, Mustardseed is a place of art and knowledge. Divided into thematic districts based on the other nations of Tanares, it is filled with places showcasing art and architecture to symbolize many aspects of the theme. Some are comical, illustrating the caricatural features of other nations, especially notable people. Many animated instruments create melodic streets, which are also thematic. The residences seem to defy physics, are sophisticated and adorned with beautiful paintings and magic items that enhance the beauty of household utensils. Their society values the individual for their education, manners, and etiquette. As a result, many unnecessary formalities arise when speaking to a gnome. The city’s crown jewel is the ‘Academy of Light,’ dedicated to deep studies in art, knowledge, and music. Despite its appearance of safety, the city harbors dangers. The city houses stone guards that can cast a secret spell to trap a person in a painting, an evil and cunning opera singer with the power to enrage non-gnomes, violent etiquette enforcers patrolling the streets, and many eccentric individuals seeking outlets for their frustrations. As lovers of sound, constant music fills the air, conveying messages when necessary. Much like the music, their artworks contain subliminal messages that often go entirely unnoticed. They boast the largest and most highly regarded music schools, The Academies of Light, which can also be found in every corner of Tanares. Closely tied to their past, in their constant quest to revive their culture and tradition, they are always organizing expeditions into the depths of the Central Sea in search of their relics and artifacts. However, there are numerous challenges, ranging from dealing with lizardfolk who have taken over some of the submerged caves to navigating the labyrinth formed by the rocks and structures that were once part of their kingdom. Occasionally, they receive assistance from the Merfolks, but most of the time, they rely on contracted groups.
